title: Music-Assist Golden Facts (Verified Church Data)
description: Hard-coded verified facts for Music-Assist brain to ensure accuracy on specific counts and policies.
content:
=== VERIFIED HYMNBOOK DATA ===
The current (green) official hymnbook of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, published in 1985, contains exactly 341 hymns.
The current Children's Songbook contains 268 songs plus several indexes.
The new hymnbook currently in production (Hymns—For Home and Church) will contain approximately 375 hymns and songs combined.

=== VERIFIED LEADERSHIP & POLICY ===
Section 19 of the General Handbook (Music) is the primary source for music policy.
Ward Choir Auditions: Auditions are NOT held for ward choirs. This is a strict policy to encourage participation. (Handbook 19.3.7.1).
Ward Music Coordinator: Oversees all music in the ward, works under the direction of the Bishopric. (Handbook 19.4.2).
Sacrament Meeting Music: Usually consists of an opening hymn, a sacrament hymn, an intermediate hymn or musical number (optional), and a closing hymn.

=== SACRAMENT MEETING MUSIC EXAMPLES ===
When suggesting specific music, frame it as an example while reinforcing that the bishopric gives final approval.
- Opening Hymn Examples: "The Spirit of God" (#2), "Redeemer of Israel" (#6). These invite the Spirit and unify the congregation.
- Sacrament Hymn Examples: "In Humility, Our Savior" (#172), "While of These Emblems We Partake" (#174). These focus on the Savior's Atonement.
- Special Musical Number Example: A Primary chorus singing "I Feel My Savior's Love" (Children's Songbook, p. 74).
- Closing Hymn Examples: "God Be with You Till We Meet Again" (#152), "On My Way Home" (#293).

=== KEY FIGURES ===
Mack Wilberg is the current Music Director of the Tabernacle Choir at Temple Square.
Ryan Murphy is the Associate Music Director of the Tabernacle Choir.

=== PERFORMANCE STANDARDS ===
Hymns should be sung at the tempo suggested in the hymnbook, though local leaders can adjust for the spirit of the meeting.
Conducting: Basic 2/4, 3/4, 4/4, and 6/8 patterns are used. The 'beat' should be clear and simple.
